title: Problem Solving
description: Problem-solving processes, algorithms and heuristics, solution techniques, flowcharts, pseudocode, decision tables and decision trees, and simple programs. The course folder holds only a reference textbook, so this course follows the NUC CCMAS outline for COS 102: facts come from that textbook (Computer Science Illuminated) where it covers a topic, and from general knowledge of the subject elsewhere.

topics.title: Computing Concepts and Types of Problems
topics.summary: A computing system is hardware, software and data working together to solve problems, organised in layers from information up to communications. Problems can be routine or non-routine, and some, such as the halting problem, cannot be solved by any program.
subtopics: Computing system: hardware, software and data
Solvable and unsolvable problems: the halting problem

topics.title: The Problem-Solving Process and Algorithms
topics.summary: Polya's How to Solve It gives four steps: understand the problem, devise a plan, carry out the plan and look back. In computing, the plan is an algorithm, developed top-down through the analysis, algorithm development, implementation and maintenance phases, while heuristics give good-enough answers without a guarantee.
subtopics: Ask questions, look for familiar things, divide and conquer
The computer problem-solving process: four phases
Definition and properties of an algorithm
Top-down design and testing an algorithm

topics.title: Problem-Solving Techniques
topics.summary: The CCMAS outline lists techniques for finding a solution, from abstraction, analogy and brainstorming to means-end analysis, root cause analysis and divide and conquer. Each suits a different kind of problem, and they are often combined.
subtopics: Trial and error and hypothesis testing
Method of focal objects and morphological analysis
Research, root cause analysis, proof, divide and conquer

topics.title: Flowcharts, Pseudocode, Decision Tables and Decision Trees
topics.summary: A solution is designed before it is coded, using pseudocode (variables, assignment, input/output, selection and repetition), flowcharts with standard symbols, or decision tables and trees when an action depends on several conditions.
subtopics: Decision tables: conditions, actions and rules

topics.title: From Algorithm to Program
topics.summary: In the implementation phase an algorithm is translated into a programming language such as Python, using assignment, input and output, conditions and loops. Count-controlled and event-controlled loops repeat work, and testing and debugging confirm that the program gives correct results.
